name: Dusky Pink
lede: Dusky Pink is a muted, slightly bluish rose, a long-running name for pinks that have lost their brightness.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files this swatch in a block, and the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 records a plate for it with a first date of 1918 [1]. The xkcd survey of 2010 used the same words, and its near-duplicates there are Old Pink, Muted Pink and Ugly Pink [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[puce]], about 4 units away [1].

In a book Dusky Pink turns up in a row of silk cocoons: Finlay lists cream white, citron yellow, yolk orange, dusky pink and chestnut brown [2]. The colors come from natural pigments in the gum that coats each cocoon, and they depend on how each worm processes carotenoids and other substances in its diet [2]. It is genetic, as eye color is in people [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a rare color in painting. Only 18 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.08 per cent, hold a color near this swatch, which makes it rarer than 72 per cent of the named colors [3]. The earliest in our archive dates from 1560, centuries before the name was first recorded, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a pigment [3].
